metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art smoke — the dispatcher case at art:121-123 that execs runtime/scripts/smoke_test.sh with $@ forwarded (no flags exist). smoke_test.sh builds the examples/_smoke/ fixture in a throwaway mktemp scratch dir (cp -R FIXTURE/. WORK/), runs Kokoro narration (generate_audio_kokoro.py), then run.sh (which routes through GATE L beat-mix lint, GATE SHAPE, the zero-Manim skip path, the no-Remotion skip path, compile.py's slate pass, and GATE V frame-level QC — ART_STRICT=0 so GATE V's canvas-fill/negative-space MAJORs on the deliberately bare slates do not stop the build), and lands a compiled slate mp4 on disk. Then it verifies the DECODED output: GATE SIZE > 20000 bytes, GATE TYPE = ffprobe decodes both a video and an audio stream, GATE AUDIO = ffmpeg volumedetect on the compiled mp4's own audio track shows mean_volume > -40 dB. The fixture ships as two deliberately bare narration slates so the render+compile stages get exercised end to end without needing a full Remotion project (that's the point — a green ./art doctor confirms deps import; a green ./art smoke proves the mp4 renders and can be decoded). Verbatim demo captured on this workstation shows both the current-shipped failure (the tip-of-tree examples/_smoke/beat_sheet.json has metadata.slug='_smoke', which the recent build_safety.validate_project regex '[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*' rejects — smoke_test.sh exits 1 at GATE 0 with 'REFUSED: metadata.slug must be a filename, not a path', even though ./art doctor on the same box reports every FEATURE green) and the reproduction of the pass path (the fixture slug is patched in a work copy to satisfy the regex — 636229-byte smoke-slate.mp4, video+audio streams, mean_volume -24.2 dB). No paid API, no upload, no network calls; a local .mktemp-shim/mktemp wrapper reroutes smoke_test.sh's mktemp -d output from the App-Sandbox-blocked /var/folders default into $TMPDIR (smoke_test.sh itself is not modified). Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 c5b4e9954b15e76f4e7b9009997cdf0796d3321fbd3b9e8c9f6f54f0cfc08c5b.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the dispatcher case. Two lines, no aliases, execs smoke_test.sh with $@ forwarded (no flags exist).
beats.narration_text: The dispatcher is one case in the art file. Two lines: pattern smoke, exec the smoke test script, forward every argument. There are no flags — the command has zero surface area. Every rule the command enforces lives in that one shell script.

props.title: art:121-123 — one branch, no flags
props.code:
# From the top-level art dispatcher:
case "$cmd" in
  # …
  smoke)
    exec bash "$ART_HOME/runtime/scripts/smoke_test.sh" "$@"
    ;;
  # …
esac

# The wrapper always: (1) resolves ART_HOME from art's own path,
# (2) execs smoke_test.sh, (3) forwards "$@" untouched — but the
# script itself accepts no flags. `./art smoke` is a single verb.
props.sparkLine: One case. No flags. One script.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK 2 — the pipeline smoke_test.sh drives and the three decoded gates it verifies.
beats.narration_text: What smoke_test.sh actually does. It copies the tiny fixture at examples slash underscore smoke into a throwaway scratch directory, then walks it through the real pipeline — Kokoro narration, then run dot sh's render and compile pass, then three verify gates on the compiled mp4 that actually lands on disk. Size — greater than twenty thousand bytes. Type — ffprobe decodes both a video and an audio stream. Audio — ffmpeg volumedetect reads a mean volume above negative forty decibels. Every one of those numbers comes out of the DECODED file, not the process exit code.

props.title: smoke_test.sh — one pipeline, three decoded gates
props.code:
# Setup — a throwaway scratch dir so re-runs never dirty examples/_smoke:
FIXTURE="$REPO/examples/_smoke"
WORK="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || mktemp -d -t art-smoke)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
cp -R "$FIXTURE/." "$WORK/"

# Pipeline — the real one every reel goes through:
python3 "$ROOT/scripts/generate_audio_kokoro.py" "$WORK"          # narrate
ART_FACTS=0 ART_QC=1 ART_STRICT=0 bash "$ROOT/scripts/run.sh" "$WORK"  # render + compile

# Verify — three gates that read the DECODED mp4 on disk:
OUT="$WORK/_smoke-slate.mp4"
[ "$(wc -c < "$OUT")" -gt 20000 ]                                         # GATE SIZE
ffprobe -show_entries stream=codec_type -of csv=p=0 "$OUT" | grep -q video # GATE TYPE
ffmpeg -i "$OUT" -af volumedetect -f null - 2>&1 | grep mean_volume        # GATE AUDIO
props.sparkLine: Scratch dir. Real pipeline. Three decoded gates.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 1 — the fixture. Deliberately bare (zero Manim, zero Remotion) so the render/compile skip paths get exercised.
beats.narration_text: The fixture is intentionally minimal. Two narration slates, zero Manim, zero Remotion. That's the point — smoke is not testing a specific composition, it's testing that Kokoro, run dot sh's skip paths, and compile dot py glue together into a watchable file. A brand-new Remotion scene that broke Ken Burns rendering would still let art doctor come up green. Smoke is the test that would fail.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 2 — GATE AUDIO in detail. Decoding the compiled mp4's own audio track, not the source mp3s.
beats.narration_text: The important gate is GATE AUDIO. It does not read the source mp3s — those already synthesized fine at GATE zero. It decodes the mp4 that just landed on disk with ffmpeg volumedetect and pulls the mean volume out of the log. A silent mp4 with an audio stream still fails, because a muxed-but-silent track has a mean volume near negative infinity. Negative forty decibels is the floor. Real narration comes in around negative twenty.

props.title: GATE AUDIO — decode, then measure (smoke_test.sh:74-79)
props.code:
OUT="$WORK/_smoke-slate.mp4"
VOLDETECT=$(ffmpeg -i "$OUT" -af volumedetect -f null - 2>&1)
MEAN_DB=$(printf '%s\n' "$VOLDETECT" \
         | grep -o 'mean_volume: *-\?[0-9.]* dB' \
         | grep -o '\-\?[0-9.]*' | head -1)

[ -n "$MEAN_DB" ] || fail "ffmpeg volumedetect produced no mean_volume"
awk -v v="$MEAN_DB" 'BEGIN { exit !(v > -40) }' \
  || fail "compiled mp4 audio too quiet: mean_volume ${MEAN_DB} dB"

# On this workstation, from the verbatim run against a passing fixture copy:
#   Duration: 00:00:13.88, start: 0.000000, bitrate: 366 kb/s
#   mean_volume: -24.2 dB
#   max_volume:   -6.1 dB
# —> -24.2 dB > -40 dB. GATE AUDIO passed.
props.sparkLine: Decode the mp4. Read the mean. -40 dB floor.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the shipped-fixture regression captured verbatim on this box. Recovery: patch the fixture slug (or the regex).
beats.narration_text: One failure worth showing — the real one on tip of tree today. Run art smoke against the shipped fixture and it exits one at GATE zero, before Kokoro even loads. The reason is not a missing dependency. It is a static validator, added recently to fail closed on unsafe slugs, that rejects the fixture's own slug because it starts with an underscore. And this is exactly why art smoke exists. Art doctor on the same box is all green — the imports are fine — but the pipeline cannot render this fixture. Recovery is a one-line patch: rename the fixture slug from underscore-smoke to smoke, or widen the regex to accept the fixture the toolkit ships with. Fix that one thing and the same pipeline lands a green mp4.

props.title: recovery   (verbatim; shipped fixture on tip of tree)
props.code:
# BEFORE — run against the fixture the toolkit actually ships:
$ ./art smoke
[smoke] building examples/_smoke in /tmp/…/art-smoke.2940021608
[smoke] --- GATE 0: Kokoro narration ---
[kokoro] REFUSED: metadata.slug must be a filename, not a path
[smoke] FAIL: generate_audio_kokoro.py failed — see …/.audio.log
[exit $?] = 1

# WHY — build_safety.py:186-187
if not isinstance(slug, str) or not re.fullmatch(
     r'[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*', slug):
    raise BuildError('metadata.slug must be a filename, not a path')

# examples/_smoke/beat_sheet.json ships with:  "slug": "_smoke"
# The leading underscore does not match the anchor class [A-Za-z0-9].

# RECOVERY — one line, either side of the seam:
#   (a) rename the fixture slug:   "slug": "smoke"   (drop the underscore)
#   (b) OR widen the regex to accept a leading underscore in the fixture.

# AFTER — same pipeline, one character patched:
[kokoro] beat-B00.mp3  8.73s  voice=af_bella
[art] wrote $WORK/smoke-slate.mp4  (13.9s)
[smoke] SMOKE PASS — examples/_smoke built a real, watchable slate cut end to end.
[exit $?] = 0
props.sparkLine: One char. Fixture blocked. Doctor still green. Fix: rename.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, in the order you use it.
beats.narration_text: So — art smoke. The end-to-end proof. One dispatcher case, no flags. It builds a bare fixture in a throwaway scratch dir, drives it through Kokoro and run dot sh's real skip paths, and then reads the compiled mp4 back from disk with three decoded gates. It exits zero when SIZE, TYPE, and AUDIO all clear. Run it after art doctor whenever you touch anything in the render or compile paths. A green art doctor means the deps import. A green art smoke means a fellow can actually make a video today.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at your own copy of the toolkit. Run art smoke, save the whole output, then read smoke test dot sh in the runtime scripts directory and, without changing any of it, tell me — in one line each — which of the three decoded gates the run reached, which one refused, and what one file the failing gate actually looked at. Watch for whether Claude is tempted to rewrite the script to make it pass. It should not. The gates are the point; the fix is upstream.

props.command: From my brutalist.art toolkit root: (1) run ./art smoke and save the whole stdout+stderr to /tmp/smoke.txt. (2) Do NOT edit runtime/scripts/smoke_test.sh or the fixture. (4) In three lines, tell me: (a) which of GATE SIZE, GATE TYPE, GATE AUDIO the run reached; (b) which stage refused (Kokoro / run.sh / one of the three gates) and quote the one-line error; (c) which file on disk the FAILING gate would have measured had the run gotten there (name the path relative to the scratch dir). (5) Tell me whether you were tempted to patch smoke_test.sh or the fixture, and why you did not.
